problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav systems rely on planar 2-D frontier maps and single-floor assumptions; floor-aware methods (MFNP, ASCENT) use layer-wise maps, map resets and rule-based floor switching that fragment the 3-D traversable space, and existing 3-D planners assume a known map without semantic exploration.
motivation: Real buildings have stairs, landings and vertically overlapping spaces, so a robot and its target may lie on different floors. Cross-floor search needs online discovery of traversable support surfaces, persistent connectivity, cheap semantic guidance without per-step LLM calls, and executable motion under a limited camera FOV.
key_idea: Maintain a unified 3-D volumetric map with a traversability layer, extract frontiers only on connected support surfaces (floors, stairs, landings), and couple this with lightweight semantic guidance (instance map + BLIP-2 value map) and a hierarchical ATSP/3-D search/trajectory-optimization planner.
insight: Representing floors, stairs and landings as one connected traversable space yields large gains on multi-floor episodes (HM3D multi-floor SR 48.7%, +15.4 over ASCENT, while the 2-D-frontier VLFM gets 0.4%), without hurting single-floor performance. The mapping ablation on one planar episode shows hybrid mapping matters: the full system needs 273/1000 steps, versus 404 without penetration-based raycasting and 614 with semantic segmentation only. Remaining failures are dominated by detector false positives and annotation errors, with step budget exhaustion rising in cross-floor cases.
method: Adaptive traversability mapping: voxel occupancy map with a geometric traversable set (2-D ray casting on the support plane) and a semantic traversable set (open-vocabulary segmentation of floor/stair/rug); switches to semantic mode when stairs are stably detected or a stair landmark is targeted, with hysteresis (N_enter/N_exit).
Incremental obstacle inflation: inflates only non-traversable occupied voxels with an anisotropic kernel (fixed xy radius, downward-only z), updating only changed voxels in O(n).
Traversable frontiers: frontier voxels on the traversable surface with headroom and a non-traversable horizontal neighbor, clustered by 26-connectivity with local AABB-based incremental updates.

FOV-aware active perception: pitches the camera down for blind-spot frontiers (d < d_blind), moves irreducible ones to a dormant set, and uses a virtual ground plane to trigger downward looking for descending stairs.

Spatial semantic guidance: probabilistic instance map (SAM 3 detections fused with positive/negative evidence, target and stair branches) plus a spatial value map from BLIP-2 image-text scores projected onto visible traversable voxels with cos² FOV weighting and reliability-weighted fusion.
Chain of exploration: open ATSP (LKH) over a lexicographically activated set (target instances > current-floor frontiers > stair landmarks) with a geometric-frontier preference term.

Foothold-guided 3-D path search and execute-review: graph search over traversable voxels with foothold-scale neighborhoods and an ESDF safety cost; odometry vs predicted pose check marks blocked voxels and replans; real robot uses an EGO-Planner-style B-spline optimizer with gradients projected to the xy plane to keep the height profile.

setting.backbone: SAM 3 (open-vocab segmentation, frozen) + BLIP-2 (image-text matching, frozen) + rule-based planner (LKH ATSP, graph search, B-spline optimization)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (79° FOV) + odometry pose; real robot adds Livox Mid-360 LiDAR with FAST-LIO2 localization
setting.action_space: 6 discrete actions in sim (forward 0.25 m, turn/look 30°, stop); continuous velocity commands via B-spline trajectory on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat (Habitat Challenge 2023 setup, HM3D and MP3D)

numbers.extra: 500 step limit; success distance 0.2 m as stated

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 real trials in villa, flat, loft, office; 300 s timeout
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Overall: 50 trials, 32 succ., SR 64.0%, AT 92.5 s, SPT 44.3%

numbers_note: HM3D single-/multi-floor breakdown (74.6/41.9 single-floor SR/SPL; 48.7/16.8 multi-floor) is given in text/figure. The HM3D/MP3D split is not named explicitly (episodes follow Habitat Challenge 2023), so 'val' is assumed.
results: TravExplorer reaches 70.0 SR / 37.2 SPL on HM3D and 48.8 / 21.1 on MP3D, beating the strongest cross-floor baseline ASCENT (65.4/33.5 and 44.5/15.5) and the strongest single-floor baseline ApexNav (59.6/33.0 and 39.2/17.8). Real-world: 32 of 50 trials successful (64.0%) on a Go2.
limitations: Rule-based system; false-positive detections and dataset annotation errors are the dominant failures (22% overall, 26% cross-floor).
Greedy exploration exhausts the step budget on long cross-floor detours (6% to 18%), and simulator reconstruction holes break frontier connectivity.
Real-world success is only 64% with no baseline comparison; ablations are qualitative or a single episode.
